title: Oliver Sacks' autistic twins who traded six-digit prime numbers

tellings.quote: one of the case reports were about these twins who are institutionalized who were autistic who played a game in which they would say prime numbers back and forth to one another

plain: Diane Powell, a guest on Jesse Michels' podcast, recalls a case report by the writer Oliver Sacks, author of the book Awakenings. She says it described autistic twins living in an institution who played a game of saying prime numbers back and forth to each other, numbers six digits long. She tells it as a hint that some minds may reach information in ways we don't understand, even mind to mind.
